title: Invocation Cost Threader: compact per-invocation cost panel & export prototype
creator: Maya Patel
description: Deliver a compact, thread-style panel in Redwood Console that surfaces token-level marginal cost for individual invocations. The 'Invocation Cost Threader' condenses per-invocation token breakdowns, attribution to prompt components and assistants, small inline sparklines, and a flexible CSV export UI. This ticket covers a high-fidelity prototype, acceptance criteria, engineering handoff notes for performance budget, and a design review runbook.
background: Customers asked for a lightweight way to inspect outlier invocations without leaving the route dashboard. Current cost tooling is page-level and heavy; analysts have to download large CSVs and stitch traces to understand which prompt parts drive cost. The Threader should give engineers and PMs a fast, scannable surface for root-cause cost analysis, and an export action that respects rollups and pricing slabs.
goals: 1) Reduce time-to-insight for per-invocation cost debugging by 60% vs current flow; 2) Provide an export that includes attribution slices (system vs user, tools vs model, KV cache hits) and pricing slab used; 3) Ensure the compact panel can be embedded in the route list and the invocation inspector without performance regression.
non_goals: Full session replay, deep token-level content inspection for privacy-sensitive content, replacing existing bulk CSV exports for large-scale billing jobs.
user_stories: As an SRE, I want a compact view that shows top token contributors per invocation so I can triage cost spikes quickly.
As a PM, I want to export a CSV that includes attribution slices and the pricing slab applied so I can validate billing anomalies.
As a Platform Engineer, I want the panel to render in under 120ms for cached invocations and under 250ms for cold invocations to meet console performance SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Compact panel appears as an inline drawer from the invocation list and as a collapsible section in the Invocation Details page.
Panel shows: total cost, token count, 3-line attribution (system/user/tool), a 6-point sparkline of token consumption, and a ranked list of top 3 prompt fragments by cost share.
CSV export modal allows toggles: include_full_prompt (on/off), attribution_granularity (summary|per-fragment), pricing_slab_column (on/off), and time_window selector.
Export CSV header matches accounting schema: invocation_id, timestamp, route, model_variant, cost_usd, tokens_total, tokens_input, tokens_output, attribution_summary, pricing_slab_applied.
Prototype validated with Design Review and Product; design changes documented and engineering acceptance recorded as tech tasks.
Rendering performance verified in a perf harness with sample payloads (small, medium, large) and falls within budget.
Accessibility: panel keyboard focusable, sparklines have aria-label summaries, color contrast passes AA.
Privacy: when include_full_prompt is enabled, export warns about PII and requires a role with 'export_sensitive' permission.
engineering_notes: Keep serialization minimal: precompute attribution aggregates server-side. UI fetch returns small diff payload: {invocation_id, cost_summary, sparkline_samples[6], top_fragments[3]}. Avoid fetching full token stream by default. Cache TTL 30s for hot invocations. CSV export job can stream; enforce 10s latency SLA for typical 1-10 invocation exports. Ensure frontend aborts if payload > 1MB and surfaces a link to bulk export job.
performance_constraints: Panel should add <= 15ms CPU to main console thread for typical render. Sparklines rendered as SVG with simplified path. Avoid third-party chart libs where possible. Mobile breakpoint collapses sparkline to numeric trend.
tradeoffs:
- Inline fragment ranking helps quick triage but requires fragment hashing server-side; adds backend compute.
- Including full prompt text improves debugging but increases PII risk and export size; gated behind an explicit toggle and RBAC.
- Pre-aggregation reduces client work but can slightly delay freshness; chosen TTL balances cost and recency.
review_feedback: PM (Diego Martinez): prefer 'Attribution breakdown' label instead of 'Cost slices' for clarity.
Engineering (Anika Rao): request field-level contract: top_fragments must include fragment_id and token_span to link to KV cache hits.
Security (Priya Singh): require export audit log and add explicit modal text about data retention for CSVs.
Design (Maya Patel): reduce visual weight of sparklines, remove outer card shadow for dense tables.
Accessibility (Jordan Lee): add keyboard shortcut to open Threader when focused on an invocation row.
decisions: 1) Server will provide 6-sample sparkline that is pre-aggregated. 2) Export requires a two-step confirmation when include_full_prompt=true. 3) Fragment attribution payload limited to top 3 fragments in-panel to keep response small; full fragments available in export only.
open_questions: Should pricing_slab_applied be normalized to a human-readable name or the internal slab_id? Product prefers name but engineering needs slab_id for reconciliation.
Do we expose KV cache hit rate per fragment in the compact panel or only in the expanded invocation view?
What is the RBAC scope name for CSV exports that include PII?
